scenes.title: Key ideas
scenes.vo: State: what a contract stores (balances, parameters). Functions change it; events log what happened. Verified source: the code published on the explorer matches what's deployed. That's good, not proof of safety. Proxy / upgradeable contracts: the address you use stays the same, but the logic behind it can be swapped. Whoever controls upgrades controls your funds' rules. Admin keys and roles: owners, guardians, multisigs; can they pause, upgrade or move funds? Timelocks: a delay between an approved change and it taking effect. Your window to exit.

lines: Does verified source code mean safe?
scenes.sub: Answer: No. It means the published code matches the deployed code.

lines: Why does a timelock matter to users?
scenes.sub: Answer: It gives time to see and exit before a change takes effect.
